primary_classification.classification_basis: The provider distinctly identified Microsoft personal-account sign-in as the affected route rather than representing the incident as a generic account, entitlement or platform state. This successful-invariant finding is limited to that access-state distinction.

assessment_boundaries: The provider confirms the affected Microsoft-personal-account sign-in route but does not disclose internal root cause or allocate responsibility between OpenAI and Microsoft components.
The token_exchange_failed string is treated as an observed symptom of the federated sign-in path, not as proof of a particular backend implementation defect.

Paid-account testimony supports an otherwise-valid-entitlement candidate condition for Verification-Dependency Access Continuity, but fallback availability differs across reports and is not generalised.
The incident is not classified merely because a third-party identity dependency caused access loss.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI reported that users signing in with Microsoft personal accounts were unable to sign in, applied mitigation and reported full recovery on 5 June 2026. Multiple contemporaneous users reported token_exchange_failed errors on Microsoft-linked accounts, including paid Plus accounts. The same user reported web-browser failure and an unsuccessful Google sign-in attempt while retaining smartphone access. The same community thread later contains subscription and usage-limit complaints, including a moderator acknowledgement of subscription investigation. Their common cause or linkage to the separate incorrect-suspension occurrence is not established.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates why federated identity dependencies and fallback state must be represented separately from account validity. A failed identity route can block practical access to an otherwise existing account without implying suspension, revocation or entitlement loss. The governance question is therefore not merely whether sign-in failed, but whether a valid or unresolved entitlement remains practically reachable through a proportionate alternate path. The public evidence establishes the dependency failure but does not establish a uniform absence of such fallback across affected users. The access-state differentiation success is local to accurate route identification. The verification-dependency question remains unresolved because fallback conditions vary; successful status discrimination does not establish continuity for every affected user. Independent external assessment supports source-bounded repair in the restoration stage. The stakeholder communication-plan outcome remains Boundary because its complete planning evidence is unavailable. The SDOS governance-degradation candidate is excluded on its specific trigger or publication timing, rather than voluntary status.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident provides a useful near-boundary case for Verification-Dependency Access Continuity. It shows that evidence of a paid entitlement plus failed federated verification can satisfy much of the class while still falling short if fallback availability is unresolved or heterogeneous. That boundary prevents VIGIL from treating every identity-provider outage as a verification-dependency governance failure.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve dimensions independently reviewed. The Microsoft personal-account sign-in route was disrupted for about seventy minutes, followed by mitigation and recovery. Individual reports describe retained access on some devices and unsuccessful alternative sign-in on others. The evidence supports S2 route-specific degradation, without assuming a working fallback for everyone or meaningful broader loss. No distinct relational or heightened-protection relationship is admitted.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The unwanted access/service behaviour directly engages the OECD repair proposition. OpenAI reported mitigation at 15:24 and full recovery at 15:58 on 5 June; the community reports preserve route-dependent disruption but do not establish uniform lack of fallback. This affirmatively supports repair in the reported restoration stage, bounded to the disclosed affected scope. It does not establish prevention of recurrence, full internal controls or every individual user outcome.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The Microsoft-personal-account identity route failed while some other device routes remained available.
